body:
Instead of introducing new meta variable, you could just clear `_custom_type_script`. The bug only happens because the custom type is not removed when the script is removed.

Alternatively you could do nothing, but the error could just tell to change the type. If we had abstract GDExtension types (is this a thing already?) and someone changed a type to be abstract, the solution would be the same (assuming the node isn't just removed from the scene).
This would mean that, unlike the current version of the PR, the dialog can't give a hint of what the old type was.
You can print the old type in the error like now. It's enough.
The part about keeping track is outdated I think.
This check is unnecessary. `remove_meta()` can handle non-existing metadata.
For some reason the meta is not loaded yet here, so it doesn't get removed. You could probably defer it?
